chance_note: Whole sweep re-run with F1/F5 shuffled within instrument and model losses randomly swapped: 0 cells pass BH. Raw p < 0.05 in the real sweep: 263 (5% of 327 = 16).
intro: 52,746 instrument-sessions, 34 instruments, 2017-2022 (log-HAR race 2018-2022; chosen σ only 2020-11 to 2022). 327 cells tested; 270 pass Benjamini-Hochberg at q 0.10; the same sweep with the fields shuffled passes 0.

Over-reaction holds across everything: lowest-σ fifth minus highest-σ fifth of range ÷ σ is +0.34σ pooled (shuffled −0.01), positive and BH-passing in all 34 instruments (+0.20 EURJPY to +0.51 GBPAUD), all 4 classes, all 5 London buckets (17-22% of each bucket's mean range), every horizon, both regimes and every year (+0.42 to +0.49).

It is a flaw of the live σ, not of ranking any noisy forecast: range ÷ forecast falls from 1.07 to 0.80 across σ deciles, but is near flat for log-HAR (0.95 to 0.94) and variance-targeted GARCH (0.94 to 0.95).

The forecast-error effect holds across classes, buckets, regimes and years (+0.14σ in 2017 to +0.39σ in 2020, shuffled −0.004), but is local in size: GBP and AUD crosses +0.40 to +0.48σ, the deep USD majors only +0.07 to +0.08σ (EURUSD, NZDUSD, USDCAD fail BH). Gold +0.12σ, barely.

The error effect is short-lived: strongest at 15 minutes (24% of mean range) and down to 13% over 5 sessions; with inputs one session older it keeps 69%, by +5 sessions it is 0. Shorter EWMA half-lives are stronger (+0.44σ at 3 sessions, +0.28 at 10, +0.13 at 45): a slope, not a tuned peak at 10.

Stop gap on the bid/ask path: a 1σ stop from the 00:00 entry is hit 35.3% after under-forecasts vs 29.7% after over-forecasts (+5.5 points, shuffled +0.1; mid path +5.4). It holds for entries at every London bucket (+5.3 to +5.8), every year (+3.0 to +7.2), both regimes, and at stop widths 0.5σ to 1.5σ (+3.9 to +5.8). Not in gold, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDCAD, EURUSD.

log-HAR beats the plain live σ almost everywhere (QLIKE 0.77 RV5, 0.89 range²; every class, regime, tercile and year), but against the chosen σ it is local to FX crosses (0.86 RV5, 0.95 range²); it loses on indices (1.07) and ties on majors and gold. Pooled vs chosen on range²: 0.97 [0.94, 1.00], short of stage 1's bar.

GARCH persistence as a half-life: median 11 sessions across instruments vs 7.5 for realised log RV5, but it ranges from 2 (GBPUSD) to 200 (AUDNZD) and jumps between quarterly refits (EURJPY 8 median, 90 last): the fitted half-life is not a stable property.
Regime caveat: 93 turbulent episodes per instrument but only 4 market-wide ones, so the regime split is close to 4 events. Descriptive only; no 2023+ data was loaded.

charts.note: Range from the bucket's first bar to its end (London time, DST-aware), ÷ σ; effect as % of that bucket's mean so buckets of different length compare. Benchmark: 0 and the shuffled row. * = both pass BH.

charts.note: 15m/1h/4h = range from the 00:00 London open; next session = range of t+1 ÷ σ of t; 5 sessions = high-low over t..t+4 ÷ σ of t. Fields are fixed at the open of t. Benchmark: 0 (shuffled session values are in the time-of-day chart). * = both pass BH.

charts.title: Vol regime (C.OG Lesson 05) and σ terciles
charts.note: Turbulent = past-only 63-session vol above 1.25× its past median for 21+ sessions. 93 turbulent episodes across 34 instruments (median 64 sessions), but only 4 market-wide episodes (≥25% of instruments at once): that is the real sample. Regime cells are bootstrapped in blocks of 64 sessions and re-ranked within regime. Over-reaction inside σ terciles is skipped (same variable). Benchmark: 0.

charts.title: Year by year, 2017-2022: over-reaction, error effect, stop gap
charts.note: Fifths re-ranked within instrument-year, so a calm year is not just 'low σ'. Stop gap = 1σ stop hit rate (bid/ask) after under-forecasts minus after over-forecasts, ×10 to share the axis (0.5 = 5 points). Benchmark: 0. Intervals in cells.csv.

charts.title: Is the over-reaction a σ flaw? Range ÷ forecast by decile of each forecast
charts.note: Each forecast is put on the range scale with a past-only expanding mean of range² ÷ forecast², 2018-2022, 34 instruments. A well-scaled forecast is flat at 1 (benchmark). A falling line = too high when high, too low when low.

charts.title: log-HAR vs the live σ and the chosen σ, by condition: QLIKE ratio
charts.note: Below 1 = log-HAR forecasts that cell's session variance better. Benchmark: 1. Chosen σ exists from 2020-08 (scaled from ~2020-11), so its column is 2020-11 to 2022 only; empty = not enough rows. On the range² yardstick vs chosen σ, pooled: 0.971 [0.938, 1.001]. HAR has home advantage on RV5.

charts.title: Per instrument: log-HAR loss ÷ plain σ and ÷ chosen σ
charts.note: Benchmark: 1. Sorted by the chosen-σ column. HAR is worse than the chosen σ on 13 of 34 instruments, and worse than plain σ on the range² yardstick on 0. * = the chosen-σ cell passes BH.

charts.title: GARCH persistence as a half-life: h = ln 0.5 ÷ ln(α+β), per instrument
names: benchmark: realised log RV5, ACF half-life
charts.note: C.OG Lesson 03. GARCH(1,1) by Gaussian MLE on NY-close daily returns, refitted each quarter on all earlier data. Median across instruments: GARCH 11 sessions vs realised 8 sessions (lag where the autocorrelation of log RV5 first drops below 0.5). The F5 error EWMA uses 10 sessions.

charts.title: Stop gap: 1σ stop hit rate after under-forecasts minus after over-forecasts
charts.note: Two-sided stop 1σ from the entry, held to 22:00. Bid/ask: a long fills at the offer and is stopped when the bid trades through; a short the reverse. Later entries use 1σ × √(past share of the day's variance still to come). Under = F5 top two fifths, over = bottom two. Benchmark: shuffled F5 and the mid path. * = BH pass.

charts.title: Plateau check 1: the stop gap across stop widths (bid/ask path)
charts.xlabel: stop width (live σ from the 00:00 entry)
charts.note: Neighbouring widths, not just 1σ. A gap that holds across widths is a plateau. Benchmark: all sessions (what σ alone implies). Median spread at 00:00 = 0.048σ. Mean R at 1σ (stop or 22:00 exit, long+short): net -0.089 under / -0.083 over; gross +0.001 / +0.004.

charts.title: Plateau check 2: error effect across EWMA half-lives and splits
charts.xlabel: half-life of the error EWMA (sessions; stage 2 used 10)
charts.note: Top minus bottom group of F5 rebuilt at each half-life. A flat run = plateau; a spike at 10 = a tuned peak. Benchmark: shuffled F5 at -0.004. Fifths: +0.437 at 3 sessions, +0.278 at 10, +0.133 at 45.

charts.title: Lesson 01 check: every input delayed by more sessions
charts.note: σ, F5 and their fifths taken k sessions earlier; the outcome stays session t. 1 = as strong as with today's inputs; 0 = gone (benchmark). At +1: over-reaction +0.414σ [+0.337, +0.498] vs +0.340 at 0; error effect +0.192 [+0.136, +0.248] vs +0.278; stop gap +3.9 pts vs +5.5. Over-reaction GROWS with delay (a staler σ is a noisier ranker); the error effect and stop gap fade to 0 by +5: they live in the last few sessions' misses.

charts.title: Real GBPUSD sessions, 2022: long at the 00:00 offer, path of the bid in σ
charts.note: Four sessions after under-forecasts (F5 top fifth) and four after over-forecasts (bottom fifth), seeded pick. Stop line at −1σ (path ends at the stop); +1σ drawn for scale. R is net: entry at the offer, exit at the bid. Benchmark: across all 2017-2022 sessions a 1σ stop is hit 32.4% of the time (bid/ask).
